blocks.text: Dohra:
The way Lord Shiva, on an impulse of emotional rush, Had blessed the demon Bhasmantar1 with a boon. Satguru Guru Nanak, in a similar inadvertent gesture, Had blessed Babur2 with a (great) boon. (1)
lines: The way Lord Shiva, on an impulse of emotional rush,
Had blessed the demon Bhasmantar1 with a boon.
Satguru Guru Nanak, in a similar inadvertent gesture,
Had blessed Babur2 with a (great) boon.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Listen to the way dear devout Gursikh readers, How the Guru had to bear great hardships for his utterances. For keeping the promise of his utterances and for the sake of his Sikhs, The Guru had to undergo many trials and tribulations. (2)
lines: Listen to the way dear devout Gursikh readers,
How the Guru had to bear great hardships for his utterances.
For keeping the promise of his utterances and for the sake of his Sikhs,
The Guru had to undergo many trials and tribulations.

blocks.text: Since the moment Guru Nanak manifested himself in human appearance, His devour Sikhs received his blessings in plenty. Whosoever showed a little bit of devotion to the Guru, Instantly was he rewarded by the Guru's grace. (3)
lines: Since the moment Guru Nanak manifested himself in human appearance,
His devour Sikhs received his blessings in plenty.
Whosoever showed a little bit of devotion to the Guru,
Instantly was he rewarded by the Guru's grace.

blocks.text: Whosoever appeared before the Divine Guru in mind pure, He had had his cherished desires fulfilled by the Guru. Whosoever sat in remembrance of the Guru at home. He, too, was rewarded by the Guru to his heart's content. (4)
lines: Whosoever appeared before the Divine Guru in mind pure,
He had had his cherished desires fulfilled by the Guru.
Whosoever sat in remembrance of the Guru at home.
He, too, was rewarded by the Guru to his heart's content.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Everyone got his cherished desires fulfilled, Whosoever sought his intercession with devotion. None went back with an unfulfilled desire, Such was the grace and beneficence of the great Guru. (5)
lines: Everyone got his cherished desires fulfilled,
Whosoever sought his intercession with devotion.
None went back with an unfulfilled desire,
Such was the grace and beneficence of the great Guru.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

At a place known by the name Rai Bhoi's Talwandi,3 Had Guru Nanak taken birth (in the human form). Wth one blessed glimpse of infant Nanak's angelic face, Had Rai Bhoi4 been blessed with a ministership at Delhi Court. (6)
lines: At a place known by the name Rai Bhoi's Talwandi,3 Had Guru Nanak taken birth (in the human form).
Wth one blessed glimpse of infant Nanak's angelic face,
Had Rai Bhoi4 been blessed with a ministership at Delhi Court.

blocks.text: Since he had worshipped the divinity in Guru Nanak, Had he been endowed with a position in the royal court. In like manner was Daulat Khan Lodhi5 Pathan blessed, Who happened to be the custodian of Sultanpur. (7)
lines: Since he had worshipped the divinity in Guru Nanak,
Had he been endowed with a position in the royal court.
In like manner was Daulat Khan Lodhi5 Pathan blessed,
Who happened to be the custodian of Sultanpur.

blocks.text: As Guru Nanak became the storekeeper of custodian's warehouses, The latter had seen through the divinity in Guru Nanak. This Pathan ruler being the husband of two wives, Both of whom had aged without having any issue. (8)
lines: As Guru Nanak became the storekeeper of custodian's warehouses,
The latter had seen through the divinity in Guru Nanak.
This Pathan ruler being the husband of two wives,
Both of whom had aged without having any issue.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hearing the fame and spiritual charisma of Guru Nanak, Both the wives came to pay their obeisance to the Guru. Both of them were blessed with a couple of sons each, Of which both these wives were greatly in need. (9)
lines: Hearing the fame and spiritual charisma of Guru Nanak,
Both the wives came to pay their obeisance to the Guru.
Both of them were blessed with a couple of sons each,
Of which both these wives were greatly in need.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

While the two were named Ghazi Khan and Gaj Masat Khan, The other two were named Meerkhan and Jaula Pathan. As these four Pathan brothers became adults, They managed to become Nawabs at the Delhi Court. (10)
lines: While the two were named Ghazi Khan and Gaj Masat Khan,
The other two were named Meerkhan and Jaula Pathan.
As these four Pathan brothers became adults,
They managed to become Nawabs at the Delhi Court.

blocks.text: Lodhi Panthas being the sovereigns at the Delhi throne, Sikandar Lodhi6 , the squint eyed, was the Pathan emperor. After his death, his son Bairam Khan7 succeeded his father, Thus occupying the Delhi throne as the next Lodhi ruler. (11)
lines: Lodhi Panthas being the sovereigns at the Delhi throne,
Sikandar Lodhi6 , the squint eyed, was the Pathan emperor.
After his death, his son Bairam Khan7 succeeded his father,
Thus occupying the Delhi throne as the next Lodhi ruler.

blocks.text: The adolescents who happened to be Bairam Khan's playmates, Were they appointed custodians of various provinces by him. As these immature adolescents failed to provide good goverance, Bairam Khan accused the Nawabs of being incompetent. (12)
lines: The adolescents who happened to be Bairam Khan's playmates,
Were they appointed custodians of various provinces by him.
As these immature adolescents failed to provide good goverance,
Bairam Khan accused the Nawabs of being incompetent.

blocks.text: Getting haughty and arrogant of royal power, Bairam Khan killed many of the elder custodians. While Meer Khan and Jaul Khan were bricked alive, Gaj Masat Khan and Ghazi Khan were, by him, slaughtered. (13)
lines: Getting haughty and arrogant of royal power,
Bairam Khan killed many of the elder custodians.
While Meer Khan and Jaul Khan were bricked alive,
Gaj Masat Khan and Ghazi Khan were, by him, slaughtered.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Feeling outraged, Rai Bhoi admonished Bairam Khan, That such cruel deeds were not worthy of an emperor. Advising the emperor, the elder Pathan reminded him, That a country could not be governed without the sane-advice of veterans. (14)
lines: Feeling outraged,
Rai Bhoi admonished Bairam Khan,
That such cruel deeds were not worthy of an emperor.
Advising the emperor, the elder Pathan reminded him,
That a country could not be governed without the sane-advice of veterans.

blocks.text: Taking it ill what was otherwise was a sane advice, Bairam Khan got Rai Bhoi slaughtered as well. It has become universally proverbial after such an incident, That a bad sovereign killed his own sage physician. (15)
lines: Taking it ill what was otherwise was a sane advice,
Bairam Khan got Rai Bhoi slaughtered as well.
It has become universally proverbial after such an incident,
That a bad sovereign killed his own sage physician.

blocks.text: Pauri:

With the assassination of Rai Bhoi, Fell state governance in Shambles. Officials deserting the royal court, Assembled for mourning on a mat. Emperor having drunk the heady (power) potion, Had turned arrogant in his youth. With the assassination of Rai Bhoi, Had all the controls gone awry. (16)
lines: With the assassination of Rai Bhoi,
Fell state governance in Shambles.
Officials deserting the royal court,
Assembled for mourning on a mat.
Emperor having drunk the heady (power) potion,
Had turned arrogant in his youth.
With the assassination of Rai Bhoi,
Had all the controls gone awry.

blocks.text: After Rai Bhoi's murder most foul, All the courtiers felt threatened. Visualising the emperor as a tyrant, They lost all hope of a dignified existence. While some deserted, others went underground, Some others hurled defiance at the ruler, While some died others withdrew from royal service, Thus the emperor lost whole of his army. (17)
lines: After Rai Bhoi's murder most foul,
All the courtiers felt threatened.
Visualising the emperor as a tyrant,
They lost all hope of a dignified existence.
While some deserted, others went underground,
Some others hurled defiance at the ruler,
While some died others withdrew from royal service,
Thus the emperor lost whole of his army.

blocks.text: Sending a message through a messenger, Daulat Khan's sons informed their dear father: That his innocent sons had been killed, By the arrogant and haughty Bairam Khan. They advised their father to flee to Kabul, Otherwise, he, too, would be eliminated. He, too, should never miss an opportunity to retaliate, If he ever had any love for his sons. (18)
lines: Sending a message through a messenger,
Daulat Khan's sons informed their dear father: That his innocent sons had been killed,
By the arrogant and haughty Bairam Khan.
They advised their father to flee to Kabul,
Otherwise, he, too, would be eliminated.
He, too, should never miss an opportunity to retaliate,
If he ever had any love for his sons.

blocks.text: He must pay his obeisance to Guru Nanak, If he wished his cherished goal to be realized. He would not fail in his endeavour, If he got himself blessed by Guru Nanak. The Guru being Omniscient about everything, He must seek Guru's intercession in his venture. He must inform the Guru about the murder of his sons, Who were born on this earth with his blessings. (19)
lines: He must pay his obeisance to Guru Nanak,
If he wished his cherished goal to be realized.
He would not fail in his endeavour,
If he got himself blessed by Guru Nanak.
The Guru being Omniscient about everything,
He must seek Guru's intercession in his venture.
He must inform the Guru about the murder of his sons,
Who were born on this earth with his blessings.

blocks.text: Getting news of the murder of his sons, Daulat Khan bolted out leaving Ludhiana. Asking for a route leading to Emnabad8 , He rushed with the speed of a fast running messenger. Doning black robes on his body, He ran for his life day and night. Remaining unmindful of feeding himself, He was obsessed with escaping from there. (20)
lines: Getting news of the murder of his sons,
Daulat Khan bolted out leaving Ludhiana.
Asking for a route leading to Emnabad8 ,
He rushed with the speed of a fast running messenger.
Doning black robes on his body,
He ran for his life day and night.
Remaining unmindful of feeding himself,
He was obsessed with escaping from there.

blocks.text: Dohra:
The spot where Guru Nanak was meditating, While sitting on a mound of rocks and pebbles, Desperate Daulat Khan fell prostrate, At the lotus feet of Guru Nanak. (21)
lines: The spot where Guru Nanak was meditating,
While sitting on a mound of rocks and pebbles,
Desperate Daulat Khan fell prostrate,
At the lotus feet of Guru Nanak.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Although the great Guru was omniscient, But he kept silent for the sake of his devotee.
He listened to Daulat Khan's plight with patience, As the latter narrated all the detailed facts. (22)
lines: He listened to Daulat Khan's plight with patience,
As the latter narrated all the detailed facts.

blocks.text: After listening to Daulat Khan's woes, the guru kept silent, Nor did he answer his pleas in haste. At this, Daulat Khan pleaded for the Guru's blessings, Placing his headgear at the Guru's feet. (23)
lines: After listening to Daulat Khan's woes, the guru kept silent,
Nor did he answer his pleas in haste.
At this,
Daulat Khan pleaded for the Guru's blessings,
Placing his headgear at the Guru's feet.

blocks.text: Since he (Daulat Khan) had sought Guru's protection, May the Guru protect him or cause him to perish. Since Bairam Khan had slaughtered the Guru's devotees, Daulat Khan was pleading before the Guru for justice. (24)
lines: Since he (Daulat Khan) had sought Guru's protection,
May the Guru protect him or cause him to perish.
Since Bairam Khan had slaughtered the Guru's devotees,
Daulat Khan was pleading before the Guru for justice.

blocks.text: The Guru, for upholding the dignity of his devout followers, Must cause the Lodhi Pahtan's rule over India to end. Since the Pathan ruler had turned cannibalistic, Pathans' sovereignty over India must be done away with. (25)
lines: The Guru, for upholding the dignity of his devout followers,
Must cause the Lodhi Pahtan's rule over India to end.
Since the Pathan ruler had turned cannibalistic,
Pathans' sovereignty over India must be done away with.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Either the great Guru himself should become a sovereign ruler, Or he should anoint his son as the new sovereign. The sovereignty over India being of great significance, The Guru must preserve it in his own household. (26)
lines: Either the great Guru himself should become a sovereign ruler,
Or he should anoint his son as the new sovereign.
The sovereignty over India being of great significance,
The Guru must preserve it in his own household.

blocks.text: Hearing this, the great Guru told Daulat Khan, That he was in no need of any sovereignty. Of what consequence was the sovereignty of India, When he had renounced millions of such sovereignties. (27)
lines: Hearing this, the great Guru told Daulat Khan,
That he was in no need of any sovereignty.
Of what consequence was the sovereignty of India,
When he had renounced millions of such sovereignties.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

It was for the task of bestowing sovereignty on others, That the Divine Lord had sent him (the Guru) in the age of Kaliyuga. Since the life of a sovereign was always a bed of thorns, The Guru experienced great happiness in meditation on the Divine. (28)
lines: It was for the task of bestowing sovereignty on others,
That the Divine Lord had sent him (the Guru) in the age of Kaliyuga.
Since the life of a sovereign was always a bed of thorns,
The Guru experienced great happiness in meditation on the Divine.

blocks.text: Pauri:

Why should he (the Guru) take over such a sovereignty, That Daulat Khan was talking about time and again? Would the people not heap ridicule upon him, For having grabbed it after forsaking it earlier? Hearing this, all hopes of Daulat Khan about, Guru's acceptance of sovereignty were dashed to the ground. After this, Daulat Khan abandoned all efforts, To press the Guru again and again to become a sovereign. (29)
lines: Why should he (the Guru) take over such a sovereignty,
That Daulat Khan was talking about time and again?
Would the people not heap ridicule upon him,
For having grabbed it after forsaking it earlier?
Hearing this, all hopes of Daulat Khan about,
Guru's acceptance of sovereignty were dashed to the ground.
After this,
Daulat Khan abandoned all efforts,
To press the Guru again and again to become a sovereign.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Thereafter, Daulat Khan made another proposal, In case the Guru refused to accept sovereignty himself.
Entreating the Guru to snatch it from the Pathans in any case, The Guru should had it over to the Mughals. (30)
lines: Entreating the Guru to snatch it from the Pathans in any case,
The Guru should had it over to the Mughals.

blocks.text: Sortha:

The Guru warned Daulat Khan to beware of the consequences, Before asking him (the Guru) to bestow it on the Mughals. Lest Daulat Khan should repent later on for his plea, Sovereignty, once bestowed on Mughals, would never get back to the Pathans. (31)
lines: The Guru warned Daulat Khan to beware of the consequences,
Before asking him (the Guru) to bestow it on the Mughals.
Lest Daulat Khan should repent later on for his plea,
Sovereignty, once bestowed on Mughals, would never get back to the Pathans.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Let the Hindus or Pathans never be the sovereigns again, So did Daulat Khan agree to the Guru's conditional proposal. Let sovereignty be taken away from the Pathans, Even though it may not return to them ever again. (32)
lines: Let the Hindus or Pathans never be the sovereigns again,
So did Daulat Khan agree to the Guru's conditional proposal.
Let sovereignty be taken away from the Pathans,
Even though it may not return to them ever again.

blocks.text: This being the only fond wish in his (Daulat Khan's) mind, Let the Guru, in his graciousness, fulfill a devotee's fond wish. The Guru ordained it to be fulfilled as Daulat Khan desired, Although the latter might regret his plea at a later stage. (33)
lines: This being the only fond wish in his (Daulat Khan's) mind,
Let the Guru, in his graciousness, fulfill a devotee's fond wish.
The Guru ordained it to be fulfilled as Daulat Khan desired,
Although the latter might regret his plea at a later stage.

blocks.text: He must proceed to Kabul post haste, In order to bring Mughal emperor Babur to India. In case Babur cherished the desire to be India's emperor, He should come and consult him (Guru Nanak). (34)
lines: He must proceed to Kabul post haste,
In order to bring Mughal emperor Babur to India.
In case Babur cherished the desire to be India's emperor,
He should come and consult him (Guru Nanak).

blocks.text: In case Babur proceeded without seeking Guru's advice, The Guru would put up an another rival against him. Hearing Guru's remarks, Daulat Khan felt so much delighted, As if a son had taken birth in his own family. (35)
lines: In case Babur proceeded without seeking Guru's advice,
The Guru would put up an another rival against him.
Hearing Guru's remarks,
Daulat Khan felt so much delighted,
As if a son had taken birth in his own family.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The way a ruler feels delighted at the defeat of an enemy, The way onset of rain drenches the drought hit parched land, The way an issueless parent rejoices at the birth of a son, So were Daulat Khan's hurt feelings assuaged by Guru's predictions. (36)
lines: The way a ruler feels delighted at the defeat of an enemy,
The way onset of rain drenches the drought hit parched land,
The way an issueless parent rejoices at the birth of a son,
So were Daulat Khan's hurt feelings assuaged by Guru's predictions.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Soon after, Daulat Khan took the road to Kabul, Donning the mantle of a mendicant on the way. Meanwhile Bairam Shah had blocked all routes to Kabul, Lest Daulat Khan should escape and reach Kabul. (37)
lines: Soon after,
Daulat Khan took the road to Kabul,
Donning the mantle of a mendicant on the way.
Meanwhile Bairam Shah had blocked all routes to Kabul,
Lest Daulat Khan should escape and reach Kabul.

blocks.text: Thereupon, Daulat Khan taking an alternative route, Somehow managed to creep into the city of Kabul. Wearing his original robes once again, He entered into emperor Babur's country. (38)
lines: Thereupon,
Daulat Khan taking an alternative route,
Somehow managed to creep into the city of Kabul.
Wearing his original robes once again,
He entered into emperor Babur's country.

blocks.text: As he failed in his attempt to seek admission to Babur's court, Daulat Khan sent a silent prayer to great Guru Nanak. The moment he sought Guru's intercession through prayer. He got into touch with Babur in a moment's time. (39)
lines: As he failed in his attempt to seek admission to Babur's court,
Daulat Khan sent a silent prayer to great Guru Nanak.
The moment he sought Guru's intercession through prayer.
He got into touch with Babur in a moment's time.

blocks.text: Babur, according a state honour to Daulat Khan, Heard the whole account about India from the latter. Disclosing all the state secrets of Delhi court to Babur, Daulat Khan revealed the complete strength of the Lodhi Pathans' Army. (40)
lines: Babur, according a state honour to Daulat Khan,
Heard the whole account about India from the latter.
Disclosing all the state secrets of Delhi court to Babur,
Daulat Khan revealed the complete strength of the Lodhi Pathans' Army.

blocks.text: Disclosing Bairam Khan's slaughter of all the seasoned custodians, He informed about Bairam Khan's appointment of adolescent custodians. The new custodians, failing to govern their states efficiently, Had started accusing their predecessors for misgovernance. (41)
lines: Disclosing Bairam Khan's slaughter of all the seasoned custodians,
He informed about Bairam Khan's appointment of adolescent custodians.
The new custodians, failing to govern their states efficiently,
Had started accusing their predecessors for misgovernance.

blocks.text: Dohra:

He had slaughtered all the higher officials of the state, Together with the Provincial custodians and ministers. In their place, he had appointed immature rustic adolescents, Giving them higher positions of state and court officials. (42)
lines: He had slaughtered all the higher officials of the state,
Together with the Provincial custodians and ministers.
In their place, he had appointed immature rustic adolescents,
Giving them higher positions of state and court officials.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The miniscule number that survived this ruler's tyranny, They, too, had lost every hope of their survival. All the feudal chiefs, too, became frustrated with the situation, Even as the Maratha custodians in the south were also replaced. (43)
lines: The miniscule number that survived this ruler's tyranny,
They, too, had lost every hope of their survival.
All the feudal chiefs, too, became frustrated with the situation,
Even as the Maratha custodians in the south were also replaced.

blocks.text: Rai Bhoi who, being the seniormost among the ministers, Was also the wisest and the most sensible among them. As he witnessed the elimination of all the senior functionaries, He realized that the state administration was going to the dogs. (44)
lines: Rai Bhoi who, being the seniormost among the ministers,
Was also the wisest and the most sensible among them.
As he witnessed the elimination of all the senior functionaries,
He realized that the state administration was going to the dogs.

blocks.text: Being the emperor's well-wisher he advised the king in good faith, That the dwarfs could never accomplish tasks worthy of giants. Neither should the great warriors deserved to be killed, Nor could the petty people accomplish the higher tasks of the state. (45)
lines: Being the emperor's well-wisher he advised the king in good faith,
That the dwarfs could never accomplish tasks worthy of giants.
Neither should the great warriors deserved to be killed,
Nor could the petty people accomplish the higher tasks of the state.

blocks.text: Episode from Satswayya9
Dohra:
How can a lowly minion of a state, Accomplish a task worthy of a giant? How can the surface of a huge war-drum, Be sewn with the skin of even one hundred rodents? (46)
lines: How can a lowly minion of a state,
Accomplish a task worthy of a giant?
How can the surface of a huge war-drum,
Be sewn with the skin of even one hundred rodents?

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Hearing this, the emperor got Rai Bhoi slaughtered, Thus putting to death his own well-wishers.
As he had slaughtered Rai Bhoi without any offence, There rose an outcry throughout his entire state. (47)
lines: As he had slaughtered Rai Bhoi without any offence,
There rose an outcry throughout his entire state.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hearing the whole account of events from Daulat Khan, Babur made up his mind to attack India. However, his minister stopped him from instant action, After deliberating thoroughly over the whole issue. (48)
lines: Hearing the whole account of events from Daulat Khan,
Babur made up his mind to attack India.
However, his minister stopped him from instant action,
After deliberating thoroughly over the whole issue.
